newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Ommeren net up, optimistic on 1997.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ommeren net up, optimistic on 1997.

text.p: Dutch shipping and tank storage firm Koninklijke van Ommeren on Thursday announced an 18 percent rise in 1996 net profit and said it was optimistic about the current year and beyond.

"For 1997, we expect Van Ommeren's main markets to continue developing relatively favourably, while substantial investments in terminals and tankers will make their first full-year contribution to results," the company said in a statement.

Total net profit rose to 94.4 million guilders ($49.8 million) from a previous 80.3 million, giving a net per share of 6.06 guilders versus 5.24. Turnover, however, dipped to 756 million guilders from 880 million.
Profits in tanker shipping improved markedly, helped by the consolidation of Chemgas, while those in tank storage and transport services declined.
Van Ommeren increased dividends by 50 cents to 2.50 guilders per share.

However, the headline profit figures were not directly comparable due to a change in accounting practices. For comparative purposes, Van Ommeren restated 1995 profit at 85.4 million guilders, equal to 5.57 guilders per share.
The company also took an 11.4 million guilder extraordinary loss in 1995, compared with no extraordinaries this year.

The results were in line with analysts' expectations but few analysts were impressed with the figures or the group's prospects. Its shares fell 1.20 guilders to 83.80 on a generally weaker Amsterdam stock market.
"With market conditions certainly not ideal, the result is a reflection of the increased stability of Van Ommeren's activities," said chairman Carel van den Driest.
Although optimistic about the prospects for this year, he was not prepared to provide a 1997 forecast range.
"The year has only just started and it is really too early to give anything firm," Van den Driest said.
However, he said expected growth in chemicals and gas shipping and storage margins had led Van Ommeren to raise its return-on-equity target, to be reached by the year 2000, from 12 to 15 percent.
"Our gradual refocus on services with higher added value has enabled us to raise the return on equity target we set several years ago," Van den Driest said.
Chemicals did not fare well, compared with an exceptional 1995, but the group believed it would be the main area of growth, particularly in Asia.
"In fact, the figures have dropped instead of risen, excluding extraordinaries. Excluding acquisitions, the decline has been larger," commented analyst Gert Jochems of NIB Strating.
"All in all, the quality of the earnings is less than the current stock price suggests," he added.
Andre Mulder of BZW said he believed there was little chance of significant improvement.
"Looking at storage and shipping, I maintain the view that growth will slow down," he said. -- Amsterdam Newsroom, + 31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040 ($ = 1.897 Dutch Guilders)
